findings.summary: Runtime policy evaluation does not enforce expiry semantics.
findings.details: S13-T03 requires kill-switch policy data with expiry and rollback/audit-ready lifecycle behavior. The durable loaders ignore expired rows, but the exported evaluateOperationPolicy helper accepts now without expiresAt and evaluates only generation and disabled state. Any subsystem using the helper directly can keep treating an expired disabled kill switch as disabled rather than falling back to the default enabled policy, so expiry semantics are not consistently enforced at the runtime policy boundary.

findings.summary: Policy mutation fencing and replay safety remain optional/current-row only.
findings.details: The internal mutation now requires an idempotencyKey, but expectedGeneration remains optional and idempotency is checked only against the current active policy. A blind update can advance the current generation without proving the operator observed it, and replaying an older accepted idempotency key after a later update is active creates another generation and audit event instead of returning the original receipt or a generation mismatch. That weakens stale-generation fencing, concurrent operator safety, and replay recovery for kill-switch changes.
